interface.signature: def numoffbt(arr: list[int], n: int) -> int

preconditions.description: The input arr is a list of integers with length exactly n.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(x, int) and x >= 2 for x in arr)
preconditions.description: Every element in arr is an integer greater than or equal to 2.
The size n is between 1 and 10^5 inclusive.
Every element in arr is at most 10^5.

postconditions.description: The return value is an integer in the range [0, 1000000006].

postconditions.expression: return_value == (sum(1 for x in arr) + sum((arr.count(x) * arr.count(y)) for x in arr for y in arr if x * y in arr)) % 1000000007
postconditions.description: The return value equals the total count of valid full binary trees modulo 1000000007, where single-node trees contribute one per array element, and three-node trees contribute the product of the counts of the two children for every pair whose product exists in the array.
